newsitem.title: CHINA: China sugar import ban to remain in 1997 - paper.
newsitem.headline: China sugar import ban to remain in 1997 - paper.

text.p: China's ban on imports of sugar for general trade will remain in place in 1997, the Economic Information Daily said on Thursday, quoting an official of the cabinet's State Planning Commission.
Agricultural officials were quoted as saying continuation of the ban was meant to stabilise sugar output.
An official of the China Sugar Association denied rumours that China would import large amounts of sugar in 1997.

The Ministry Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation suspended imports of sugar for general trade in 1996 to curb huge losses by the sugar industry in the wake of rampant smuggling and oversupply, the newspaper said.
Sugar imports for reprocessing are still allowed.
Sugar output in the 1996-97 season was forecast at 6.6 million tonnes, the newspaper said.

Total sugar supply was estimated at 7.3 million tonnes, with 700,000 million tonnes imported from Cuba in 1996 and 1997, the newspaper said. Imports from Cuba are allowed under a special government-to-government trade programme.
China consumes about 7.0 million tonnes of sugar a year.
